extraction.citation: Criqui L (2015). Infrastructure urbanism: Roadmaps for servicing unplanned urbanisation in emerging cities. Habitat International 47:93-102.
extraction.country: Peru (Lima: water and sanitation) and India (Delhi: electricity)
extraction.service_provider: Sedapal, the public water and sanitation utility of Lima; three private electricity distribution companies in Delhi
extraction.regulatory_model: Peru: a 1996 property-formalisation policy made a land title a prerequisite for basic services; a 2006 law (Ley 28687) made an 'attestation of possession' issued by the district municipality a sufficient document to apply; a 2006 emergency declaration for the sanitation sector (Decreto supremo 020-2006, Ley 28870) cut investment approval from three steps to one; a community layout plan, stamped by the municipality, is required in practice (not legally obligatory) by municipalities and utilities since 2006
extraction.population: residents of unplanned (informal, self-help) settlements: about 70% of the 9 million inhabitants of Lima and about 75% of the 22 million of Delhi
extraction.sample_size: Two comparative case studies (the Lima water and sanitation utility; the Delhi electricity distributors) based on document and policy analysis, two six-month on-site investigations in 2012 and 2013, about 30 semi-structured interviews with professionals in each sector and more than 40 with urban developers and civil-society members in each city; only the Lima case concerns water and sanitation
extraction.legal_status: unplanned settlements outside planning and land-use rules and often off the official maps; de facto rather than formal tenure
extraction.effect_measure: qualitative comparative case study; no effect estimate (the coverage figures are context)
extraction.effect_estimate: Lima's utility extended water and sanitation to unplanned settlements through technical alternatives (progressive community-run mini-networks, condominial systems 2002-2008) and, above all, institutional adjustments: the 1996 titling policy had made a land title a prerequisite for services and created a backlog of demand; the 2006 law then made a simple attestation of possession sufficient, the 2006 emergency declaration cut approval steps from three to one, and a community layout plan became the working map for utilities and municipalities. Connection rose from about 75% (water) and under 60% (sanitation) in 1990 to 93.4% and 91.7% in 2013. The author calls these institutional adjustments key facilitating factors, but the coverage figures are not attributed to any one rule, and a 2006 government programme of conventional, supply-oriented projects was criticised as inflexible. Coordination deficits between actors persist.
extraction.extraction_sample_size: about 30 + 40 interviews per city and two six-month field investigations (2012, 2013)
extraction.model_type: qualitative comparative case study (sociotechnical and politico-institutional analysis)
extraction.study_design: comparative qualitative case study (document and policy analysis, field investigation, interviews)
extraction.risk_of_bias_rating: CASP Qualitative per-item (appraised 2026-10-13 on the full text): 1(aims)=Yes; 2(qual approach)=Yes; 3(design)=Yes (two cases chosen because the utilities are catching up with unplanned urbanisation; the non-comparability of a water and an electricity case is acknowledged); 4(recruitment)=Can't tell (interviewee types and numbers are given, selection is not described); 5(data collection)=Yes (documents, two six-month field investigations, about 30 sector interviews plus more than 40 with developers and civil society per city, observation); 6(researcher-participant)=Can't tell; 7(ethics)=Can't tell (no ethics statement located); 8(analysis rigor)=Can't tell (no analysis procedure described); 9(findings)=Yes; 10(value)=Yes (instruments for servicing unplanned settlements). Per CASP's own guidance no composite score is computed.
extraction.selection_bias: Moderate (positive-case selection: utilities that are catching up with unplanned urbanisation, a choice the author states)
extraction.measurement_bias: Moderate (documents and interviews; the interview counts are stated)
extraction.reporting_bias: Moderate (the author states that positive initiatives are more inspiring than recurring critiques; difficulties are reported but not weighted)
extraction.legal_measurement_quality: moderate (the instruments are named and dated: 1996 titling policy, Ley 28687, Decreto supremo 020-2006, Ley 28870; their effects are interpreted from interviews and secondary sources, not measured)
extraction.outcome_measurement_quality: moderate (Lima coverage figures are context; extension mechanisms are described qualitatively)
extraction.figure: Fig. 1 (Sedapal network extension); Fig. 4 (community layout plan, Lima)
extraction.section: Full text (journal article, 10 pages): Introduction; Case studies: contexts and method; Sociotechnical innovations to adapt to sociospatial irregularity; Institutional creativity to compensate for informality (regulatory adjustments; addressing and bricolage); Coordination deficits and promising policy instruments; Conclusion
extraction.exact_location: Methods paragraph (p. 94); Lima technico-social intervention (pp. 95-96); 'Off-the-rules: regulatory adjustments and design' (pp. 96-97); layout plan (pp. 97-98)
extraction.extraction_note: New inclusion by the PI's A16 adjudication of 2026-10-13 (narrow reading of criterion 2; the Lima water and sanitation component is rule-type), extracted from the full-text PDF in the researcher's Drive (Habitat International 47:93-102, 10 pages, read as text). The paper covers two sectors: only the Lima water and sanitation case is in scope, the Delhi case is electricity. No effect_sizes.csv row (qualitative). The text was read through the discussion of coordination deficits; the last page was read for the conclusions only in outline.

evidence_map.evidence_level: Single-study evidence: a comparative qualitative case study (document analysis, two six-month field investigations in 2012-2013, interviews) of how utilities extend networks into unplanned settlements; the Lima water and sanitation case (land title prerequisite 1996, attestation of possession 2006, sanitation emergency declaration 2006, community layout plan) is in scope, the Delhi case is electricity; read in full text 2026-10-13.
evidence_map.institutional_context: Lima: land-title prerequisite for services (1996), attestation of possession (2006), emergency declaration for the sanitation sector (2006), community layout plan; fragmented authorities
